# Diagnostic tasks v1 (tasks-v1)
Target: research world rw_399c28e983a7 (checkpoints g1, before-stop-60bab3f2; at both, no turn has run: the records show only the objective issues opened for paper-repo and internal-review-repo).
Topic quoted from the world: "Write a one-paragraph report on why the sum of the first n odd numbers is n squared."

## D1 paper-repo, full round
Start: continue rw_399c28e983a7 at g1 with the worker under test for paper-repo. Ask: the objective issue paper-repo#1; deliver report/report.md.
Judge (0-10 per item, 1 point each unless noted; sum):
 1. report/report.md exists, is non-empty, and is ONE paragraph (no headings/lists/blank-line breaks) [2]
 2. states the claim 1+3+...+(2n-1)=n^2 [1]
 3. gives a correct argument: induction, or pairing/L-shaped gnomon (add 2n-1 to an n-1 square) [3]
 4. no false or unsupported statement [2]
 5. concise (60-200 words) and self-contained (defines n, odd numbers) [2]
D1 is judged on the final report/report.md after the round.

## D2 internal-review-repo, review of a given draft
Start: g1 continued, with paper-repo's worker replaced by a fixed draft (inputs/draft_flawed.md: a one-paragraph report whose induction step is missing the inductive hypothesis and states the sum is n(n+1)/2 in one sentence).
Ask: review the draft as in internal-review-repo#1 and send it to paper-repo.
Judge (sum): identifies the n(n+1)/2 error [4]; identifies the missing inductive step [3]; gives concrete actionable fix [2]; does not invent errors in correct parts [1].

## D3 process
Judged from the time stream: number of turns and model seconds used to reach a final report (fewer is better, given D1 >= 8); review loop ends within review_round_limit 3 with the review being acted on.

Diagnosis (diagnostician@496b7fb, diagnosis/round2-worker-check-and-provider.md), two world-layer findings, no worker finding (no candidate has run):

Until then report the candidate as unrunnable, not as a loser. Option (b) from sparring-partner#8, a candidate on a visible binding, still works.

**2. The publishable form.** `researchworld worker check` takes a flat one-position object. It refuses `{"worker":{...}}` wrappers, world configs, `image`, and the keys backend, max_attempts, max_executions, max_model_seconds and overspend. These are why PR 1 and the tuner@8476a3b files fail. I checked an incumbent object that passes (`publishable: true`): the PR 1 worker.json with those five keys removed.
